newsitem.title: USA: National Semi Q2 book to bill above 1.1.
newsitem.headline: National Semi Q2 book to bill above 1.1.

text.p: National Semiconductor Corp Thursday said sales and new orders for the second quater ended November 24 were up sharply from the first quarter, and its book to bill ratio was above 1.1
In a statement, the company said sales for the most recent quarter were $661.5 million, down from $711.6 million in the second quarter of fiscal 1996 but up from $566.1 million in the first quarter.

"The strength of sales and new order rates in October and November is encouraging, but we'll wait until after the holidays to take the cork out of the bottle," Brian Halla, president and chief executive officer said. "Although our book-to-bill ratio was above 1.1 for the second quarter and customers clearly are entering the new year with very low inventory levels, we would be surprised if orders continue as strong throughout the holiday season -- happily surprised."
National Semiconductor reported net income of $29.5 million or $0.21 a share for the second quarter of fiscal 1997, compared with $79.8 million or $0.57 a share a year ago.

The company said it increased shipments in September and October by reducing die bank inventories without significantly increasing new wafer starts until November. This held the overall wafer fab capacity utilization to 67.4 percent.
The company said second quarter worldwide bookings were seasonally up almost 30 percent over the first quarter and were up more than 15 percent compared with last year.
"This was the first quarter in a year that bookings grew over the comparable quarter of the previous year," the company said.

"September orders were flat compared with August, while October orders grew approximately 25 percent over September. November orders continued the strong October rate. All three months improved over last year's levels," the company said.

Local Area Network orders led the company in overall size and rate of improvement over the first quarter. Strong market acceptance of the company's video display products resulted in significant growth in this area, it said. National Semiconductor said the personal computer and wireless telephone markets also grew strongly over last year.

In addition, analog multimarket products and Fairchild product line orders were up sharply as customers completed their component inventory corrections. Bookings grew in all regions compared with both the first quarter and last year's second quarter, with book-to-bill ratios above 1.00, the company said.
